process_area.title: Field Organization, Territory Design & Regional/District Store Management

value_stream.name: Field Retail Operations, Regional/District Management & Multi-Store Retail Execution Network

fields.Owner: VP Store Operations / Director Field Retail Operations
fields.Participants: Strategy (VS-33), Store Ops (VS-07), HR (VS-103/VS-102), LP (VS-23), Finance FP&A (VS-17.4), IT (VS-27), CX (VS-13), Facilities (VS-138)
fields.Trigger: Strategy refresh (VS-33); new CEO/COO; format evolution; major footprint change

workflows.name: Field Retail Operations Strategy, Charter & Operating-Model Design

Automation Opportunity: - Span-of-control / workload modeling from store count, sales, complexity; decision-rights-matrix templating
Controls: - CTL-761 (ensure controlled execution — Field Organization, Territory Design & Regional/District Store Management (PA-177.1).)
- CTL-761: operating model leadership-approved (VS-36); cost envelope FP&A-validated; KPIs tied to VS-33 corporate scorecard
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-07 (store ops), VS-103.3 (workforce planning), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-36 (governance); W5106 (territory), W5107 (staffing), W5127 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Span-of-control risk**: Too many stores per manager → shallow visits, missed signals; mitigated by data-driven span modeling and the W5106 territory design
- **Disconnect risk**: Field model mis-aligned to strategy/growth (new-format stores unsupported); mitigated by step-2 strategy linkage
- **Accountability risk**: Ambiguous decision rights store-vs-field-vs-HQ → slow issues; mitigated by the decision-rights matrix
System Touchpoints: - Strategy/FP&A (VS-33/VS-17.4); store ops (VS-07); workforce planning (VS-103.3); field analytics dashboard (W5127); governance (VS-36); IT (VS-27)

steps.activity: Set the field-operating model: span-of-control philosophy (stores-per-manager), the regional/district/area hierarchy, the visit cadence standard, the decision-rights matrix (store-vs-field-vs-HQ), and the field KPIs (comp sales, standards-compliance %, turnaround success, store-hotline resolution time)
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / VP Store Operations

steps.activity: Align the field model to strategy & growth: coverage of the 200-store six-region footprint, the 10–15 new-store/year ramp (links VS-37), remodel-program field support (VS-109), and the omnichannel/marketplace store role (VS-10/VS-60)
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Strategy

steps.activity: Govern & approve: leadership sign-off (VS-36), the field org-cost envelope with FP&A, and the entity placement with HR/Legal
steps.r: VP Store Operations / FP&A / HR

fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), Strategy (VS-33), HR (VS-103), Supply Chain/DC (VS-02/VS-04 — DC catchment), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Annual review; new-store openings (VS-37); store closures (VS-59); workload imbalance

workflows.name: Regional/District Territory Design, Alignment & Store-Group Assignment

Automation Opportunity: - Workload-based territory optimization (sales/store-count/complexity/travel); auto-flag of imbalance
Controls: - CTL-761 (ensure controlled execution — Field Organization, Territory Design & Regional/District Store Management (PA-177.1).)
- CTL-761: territory design data-driven & balanced; assignments reflected in location-hierarchy master (VS-29); re-balance threshold governed
Cross-references: - links to VS-29 (location master), VS-04/VS-02 (DC catchment), VS-103.3 (workforce planning); W5105 (strategy), W5107 (staffing), W5109 (P&L/grading)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Workload-imbalance risk**: One manager over-loaded → missed visits/turnarounds; mitigated by workload-based design + quarterly re-balance
- **Travel-load risk**: Island geography → excessive travel time/cost; mitigated by geographic clustering & DC-catchment alignment
- **Master-data risk**: Store→manager assignment stale in systems → reporting/visit errors; mitigated by step-2 system master update
System Touchpoints: - Location hierarchy / org master (VS-29); DC catchment (VS-04/VS-02); analytics (VS-28); workforce planning (VS-103.3); field dashboard (W5127)
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks annual territory design + per-event re-alignment

steps.activity: Design territories by workload & geography: stores-per-manager target, geographic clustering (island/region), DC catchment alignment (links VS-04 4-DC footprint), drive-time/travel-load balancing, and the regional/district naming convention
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Strategy

steps.activity: Assign stores to territories: per-store group assignment, manager allocation, the transition plan for re-alignments, and the system master update (location hierarchy)
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Store Ops / IT

steps.activity: Validate balance & re-balance triggers: workload equity check (sales, store count, complexity, new-store load), the re-alignment threshold policy, and the quarterly balance review
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Analytics

fields.Participants: HR/TA (VS-121), Workforce Planning (VS-103.3), Store Ops (VS-07), FP&A (VS-17.4), Total Rewards (VS-102)
fields.Trigger: Annual workforce plan (VS-103.3); territory re-alignment (W5106); growth ramp
fields.Volume: ~6 regional + ~10–15 district managers + ops-standards/LP field staff (~44 field-management roles)

workflows.name: Field Organization Staffing, Span-of-Control & Regional-Manager Workforce Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Demand-vs-supply workforce modeling; span-of-control benchmarking; succession-bench visibility
Controls: - CTL-761: workforce plan FP&A-budgeted; span within policy; succession bench documented (VS-19.1)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103.3 (workforce planning), VS-121 (TA), VS-19.1 (succession), VS-102 (rewards); W5106 (territory), W5108 (onboarding), W5112 (comp)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-staffing risk**: Too few managers for the footprint → shallow coverage; mitigated by demand forecast + growth buffer
- **Bench-depth risk**: No successor ready when a manager exits → coverage gap; mitigated by succession planning (VS-19.1)
- **Cost risk**: Over-staffed field org vs sales; mitigated by FP&A envelope + span discipline
System Touchpoints: - Workforce planning (VS-103.3); TA/recruitment (VS-121); succession (VS-19.1); total rewards (VS-102); FP&A (VS-17.4)

steps.a: Director Field Retail Operations / VP Store Operations
steps.activity: Forecast field-org demand: managers needed for 200 stores + 10–15 new-store/yr growth, attrition/backfill (15–20% industry turnover), and the supporting ops-standards/LP field complement
steps.r: HR / Director Field Retail Operations

steps.activity: Set the span-of-control & structure: stores-per-manager, layers (region/district/area), the ops-standards and LP field reporting lines, and succession bench depth
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / HR

steps.a: Director Field Retail Operations / VP Store Operations
steps.activity: Execute the talent supply plan: internal pipeline/succession (links VS-19.1), external recruitment (VS-121), and the budget with FP&A/Total Rewards
steps.r: HR / TA / FP&A / Total Rewards

fields.Participants: L&D (VS-19.4), HR (VS-103), existing Regional Managers (mentor), LP (VS-23), Finance/HR for multi-store P&L literacy
fields.Trigger: New manager hire/promotion (VS-121/VS-19.1); role-change; capability gap

workflows.name: Regional/District Manager Onboarding, Certification & Capability Building

Automation Opportunity: - Onboarding/certification journey in LMS; competency checklist; mentor pairing
Controls: - CTL-761: structured onboarding complete before solo territory; audit competency certified; ethics/LP certification (VS-23/VS-86)
Cross-references: - links to VS-19.4 (L&D), VS-123 (certification), VS-23/VS-86 (ethics/LP); W5107 (staffing), W5114 (visit/audit), W5115 (coaching), W5119 (best practice)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Time-to-productivity risk**: New manager slow to coverage → territory gap; mitigated by structured onboarding + mentor
- **Inconsistent-audit risk**: Untrained auditor → unreliable standards scores; mitigated by competency certification
- **Conduct risk**: Field discretion (overrides, exceptions) mis-used; mitigated by ethics/LP certification (VS-23/VS-86)
System Touchpoints: - L&D/LMS (VS-19.4); certification/competency (VS-123); field dashboard (W5127); ethics/LP (VS-23/VS-86); coaching tools (W5115)
Time Estimate: - ~4–8 weeks onboarding per new field manager

steps.activity: Run the structured onboarding: field-ops orientation, the store-visit/standards-audit method (W5114), the multi-store P&L/grading model (W5109), systems training (field dashboard, W5127), and the decision-rights matrix
steps.r: L&D / Director Field Retail Operations / Mentor

steps.activity: Certify the field-leader competencies: retail-standards audit competency, coaching conversation (W5115), turnaround-diagnosis (W5111), ethics/LP/ABC conduct (links VS-23/VS-86), and the certification assessment
steps.r: L&D / LP / Director Field Retail Operations

steps.activity: Sustain capability: ongoing field-leader development, peer cohort, the field best-practice forum (W5119), and the periodic recertification
steps.r: L&D / Director Field Retail Operations

fields.Participants: FP&A (VS-17.4), Store Ops (VS-07), Regional/District Managers, Strategy (VS-33), CX (VS-13)

workflows.name: Multi-Store P&L Governance, Store Grading & Performance Tiering

Automation Opportunity: - Multi-store performance dashboard with auto-tiering; benchmark ranking; watch-list auto-flag
Controls: - CTL-761: P&L data reconciled to VS-17.4 close; multi-metric grading; independent assurance cross-check (VS-146); action-plan accountability
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4 (FP&A/store P&L), VS-33 (strategy), VS-13 (CX), VS-23 (shrink); W5114 (standards), W5111 (turnaround), W5127 (dashboard)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-tiering risk**: Stale/inaccurate data → wrong tiering → mis-allocated attention; mitigated by monthly data refresh & multi-metric grading
- **Gaming risk**: Field managers game the standards score; mitigated by independent assurance (VS-146 mystery shopping)
- **Inaction risk**: Tiering without follow-through → no improvement; mitigated by tier-based action plans + executive review
System Touchpoints: - FP&A/store P&L (VS-17.4 — W1405 store P&L); analytics (VS-28); standards score (W5114); CX (VS-13); shrink (VS-23); field dashboard (W5127)

steps.activity: Compile multi-store performance: per-store P&L contribution, comp sales, margin, shrink (VS-23), inventory turn, standards-compliance score (W5114), CX score (VS-13), and the field-manager portfolio roll-up
steps.r: FP&A / Analytics / Director Field Retail Operations

steps.activity: Grade & tier stores: A/B/C/D tiering (or equivalent), the watch-list flagging of underperformers, and the regional/peer benchmark ranking
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / FP&A

steps.activity: Drive action: tier-based action plan (turnaround W5111 for D-tier, growth plan for A-tier), accountability to the field manager, and the executive review
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Regional Managers

fields.Owner: Director Field Retail Operations / Store Opening (VS-37)
fields.Participants: Store Opening (VS-37), Store Ops (VS-07), HR/Training (VS-19.4/VS-37.2), Merchandising (VS-01), IT (VS-27), Facilities (VS-138)

workflows.name: New-Store Stabilization, Maturity Ramp & Field Handover Support

Automation Opportunity: - 30/60/90 milestone tracker; maturity-ramp benchmark vs peer openings; auto-flag of off-track ramp
Controls: - CTL-761 (ensure controlled execution — Field Organization, Territory Design & Regional/District Store Management (PA-177.1).)
- CTL-761: stabilization plan documented; KPI-gated steady-state sign-off; lessons-learned captured (VS-133)
Cross-references: - links to VS-37 (store opening), VS-109 (remodel — analogous field support), VS-130 (acquisition); W5109 (P&L), W5113 (visit cadence), W5122 (escalation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Slow-ramp risk**: New store underperforms maturity curve → stranded investment; mitigated by 30/60/90 milestones + intensive support
- **Handover-gap risk**: Premature handover to steady-state → regression; mitigated by KPI-gated sign-off
- **Knowledge-loss risk**: Lessons not captured → repeat mistakes at next opening; mitigated by step-3 lessons-learned
System Touchpoints: - Store opening (VS-37); store ops (VS-07); field dashboard (W5127); training (VS-19.4); escalation (W5122); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Plan field stabilization: assign a field sponsor, set the 30/60/90-day stabilization milestones (sales ramp, standards compliance, CX, shrink, staff retention), and the intensive visit cadence for the ramp period
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Store Opening

steps.activity: Execute stabilization support: intensive field visits, hands-on standards/merchandising help, staff coaching, escalation of issues to HQ support center (W5122), and weekly stabilization reporting
steps.r: Regional/District Manager / Director Field Retail Operations

steps.a: Director Field Retail Operations / VP Store Operations
steps.activity: Hand over to steady-state: maturity-ramp sign-off (meets steady-state KPIs), transition from intensive to standard cadence, and the post-stabilization lessons-learned
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Store Ops

fields.Participants: Regional/District Manager, Store Manager (VS-07), FP&A (VS-17.4), LP (VS-23), CX (VS-13), HR (VS-103/VS-84), Merchandising (VS-01)
fields.Trigger: D-tier grading (W5109); comp-sales decline; shrink spike; CX collapse; incident

Automation Opportunity: - Distressed-store early-warning (auto-flag on multi-metric decline); turnaround-plan template; milestone tracker
Controls: - CTL-761 (ensure controlled execution — Field Organization, Territory Design & Regional/District Store Management (PA-177.1).)
- CTL-761: structured diagnosis documented; turnaround plan leadership-approved; weekly governance; closure decision per VS-59 criteria
Cross-references: - links to VS-59 (store closure), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-23 (shrink), VS-13 (CX), VS-84 (labor relations); W5109 (grading), W5113 (visits), W5122 (escalation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-diagnosis risk**: Treating symptoms not root cause → wasted effort; mitigated by structured multi-dimensional diagnosis
- **Drift risk**: Turnaround plan not executed → no improvement; mitigated by weekly governance + escalation
- **Closure-delay risk**: Holding a non-viable store too long → losses compound; mitigated by the explicit closure option (VS-59)
System Touchpoints: - FP&A (VS-17.4); analytics (VS-28); standards (W5114); CX (VS-13); shrink (VS-23); HR (VS-103/VS-84); field dashboard (W5127); escalation (W5122)
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks diagnosis + 90–180 days execution per turnaround

steps.activity: Diagnose root cause: structured diagnosis across sales/traffic/conversion, merchandising/assortment, operations/standards, people/leadership, shrink/loss, CX, and local market/competition
steps.r: Regional/District Manager / Director Field Retail Operations / FP&A

steps.a: Director Field Retail Operations / VP Store Operations
steps.activity: Build the turnaround plan: 90-day action plan with owners, milestones, KPI targets, the resource asks (HQ support, capital, staffing), and the governance cadence
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Store Manager / Functional Leads

steps.activity: Execute, monitor & decide: intensive execution + weekly review, escalation of blockers (W5122), and the continue/extend/close decision vs the closure option (VS-59)
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / Store Manager

fields.Owner: Director Field Retail Operations / Total Rewards (VS-102)
fields.Participants: Total Rewards (VS-102), FP&A (VS-17.4), HR (VS-103), Store Ops (VS-07), Compliance (VS-118/VS-22)
fields.Trigger: Annual comp cycle (VS-102); incentive plan design; recognition program

workflows.name: Field Compensation, Incentive & Multi-Store Performance Recognition

Automation Opportunity: - Verified-data payout calculation; balanced-scorecard incentive engine; recognition platform
Controls: - CTL-761 (ensure controlled execution — Field Organization, Territory Design & Regional/District Store Management (PA-177.1).)
- CTL-761: incentive balanced multi-metric; standards score independently assured (VS-146); payout verified & approved
Cross-references: - links to VS-102 (total rewards), VS-19.2 (payroll), VS-118 (integrity), VS-146 (assurance); W5109 (performance), W5114 (standards), W5119 (recognition)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Gaming risk**: Incentive tied to self-reported standards score → gaming; mitigated by independent assurance (VS-146) and integrity controls
- **Wrong-metric risk**: Incentive on sales-only → margin/shrink/CX neglected; mitigated by balanced multi-metric design
- **Pay-integrity risk**: Payout errors → cost/disputes; mitigated by verified-data calculation & approval
System Touchpoints: - Total rewards (VS-102); payroll (VS-19.2); performance data (W5109/W5114); FP&A (VS-17.4); recognition (W5119)

steps.a: Director Field Retail Operations / Total Rewards Director
steps.activity: Design field-leader incentive: the multi-store comp-sales / margin / standards-compliance / portfolio-P&L incentive structure, the threshold/cap, and the integrity controls (no gaming of standards score)
steps.r: Total Rewards / Director Field Retail Operations / Compliance

steps.a: Director Field Retail Operations / Total Rewards Director
steps.activity: Administer & pay: calculate payouts from verified performance data (W5109/W5114), approve, and process via payroll (VS-19.2)
steps.r: Total Rewards / FP&A / Payroll

steps.activity: Run recognition: top-performer recognition, the field-best-practice forum (W5119), and the periodic non-monetary recognition
steps.r: Director Field Retail Operations / HR
